texts: what each layer depends on, what the planner outputs, and the HACC post-map
arm M2b, two training seeds (s0, s1)  |  banked checkpoints and banked per-window plans, CPU re-read  |  T1-class open loop (NOT closed loop); interventions are diagnostics
Every layer also reads the NAV command (FOLLOW / TURN_L / TURN_R and the distance to the next turn), ego motion and the camera tokens.
1   Who listens to what?  Which input does each layer actually depend on (causal, one input swapped at a time)?
2   Does the trajectory follow the nav command, and through which layer?  (nav injected at one layer at a time)
3   What does the planner's output look like against the human path, the kinematic prior P10 and the earlier blends?

4   NEW in v3:  does HACC, a zero-training per-step blend of the model's plan and P10, dominate P10 at both training seeds, and
where does the gain come from?

5   NEW in v4 (chapter 7):  T1-kin, the model run on its OWN executed motion, replanning every 2 s (self-action OPEN loop, NOT
closed loop): does HACC still beat the floor run the same way, and which gap stays open?

6   NEW in v5 (chapter 8):  DAgger: the model fine-tuned on a fraction p = 0.1 of its OWN rolled-out states (human labels),
against the same fine-tune without them (T1-kin, NOT closed loop): do T's decisions survive its own motion?

Windows are declared by a rule before anything is rendered: chapters 3-6 (SELECTION_V2.md) JUNCTION #1131, CURVE #654, NO-TURN #763, FAILURE #2158; chapter 7 (SELECTION_V4.md)
those four plus three draws; chapter 8 (SELECTION_V5.md) seven windows chosen by the DAG - DAG-0 difference.  Panels: seed 0.

Tier of chapters 1-6: T1-class open loop (own held outputs; NOT closed loop).  The model reads its own held outputs; nothing it does feeds back into the scene.  Interventions
replace an input: they show dependence, not skill.  Chapters 7-8: T1-kin, self-action OPEN loop.
Baseline: P10 is the programme's own kinematic floor, DAG-0 the same fine-tune without the lever; neither is the state of the art, and no external benchmark is shown.
Estimator: paired episode-cluster bootstrap, B = 2,000, 141 episodes (answers 'another draw of EPISODES' only); training variance = the two seeds side by side; inference is deterministic.
